# Generated by gen_p12.py - do not edit by hand.
source Python integers and the published curve orders (SEC 2 / FIPS 186-5); OpenSSL (cryptography) confirms the order, and that d and n - d give negated public keys
seed 1
compare records
requirement R1 A key from B to n - B, both ends included, gets `ok`
requirement R2 Zero and any value of n or more get `out-of-range`; zero gets it although it is also below B
requirement R3 A key below B gets `weak`, including the eight values from the incident; B - 1 is the largest of them
requirement R4 A key above n - B gets `weak`, because d and n - d are as easy to guess as each other; n - 1 is the largest of them
requirement R5 Each curve uses its own order, byte length and bound B (2^128 for P-256, 2^192 for P-384)
requirement R6 For a `draw` line, the generator draws, validates and redraws after every rejection, whatever its reason, and the answer is the first block that passes
requirement E2E One input mixes validate and draw lines on both curves, with every verdict
